title: Lemon and thyme shortbread
subtitle: buttery, crisp shortbread biscuits with lemon zest and fresh thyme
excerpt: Lemon and thyme shortbread is a classic shortbread mixture of butter, flour, and icing sugar with fine lemon zest and a small amount of fresh thyme leaves worked into the dough. The thyme adds a subtle herbal note that works with the lemon rather than against it. The dough is chilled before rolling and stamping, keeping it firm and easy to handle.
sourceNotes: Shortbread is a Scottish biscuit with records dating from at least the 16th century, originating from medieval biscuit bread. The classic ratio of flour, butter, and sugar has remained largely unchanged. Flavouring shortbread with citrus zest and herbs is a modern variation that became popular in British home baking and patisserie from the 1990s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked biscuits in a single layer, then store in a container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.batchNotes: The dough can be made in a double batch, rolled into logs, and frozen for baking as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Biscuits keep in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Lemon and thyme shortbread uses the classic shortbread ratio of one part icing sugar to two parts butter to three parts flour, with lemon zest and fresh thyme leaves worked in. Shortbread should not be overworked; mix only until the dough comes together. Chilling before rolling keeps the dough manageable and prevents the biscuits from spreading or losing their stamped shape during baking. The oven temperature is deliberately low so the biscuits dry out to a sandy, crisp texture rather than colouring much.

Put the flour, icing sugar, salt, lemon zest, and thyme leaves in a large bowl. Add the cold butter cubes. Rub the butter into the flour mixture with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolks and mix until the dough just comes together into a ball. Do not overwork.
Flatten the dough into a disc, wrap in cling film, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160 degrees C (fan 140 degrees C / gas 3). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Roll the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface to 5 mm thick. Stamp into rounds or fingers with a cutter or knife. Place on the prepared trays. Prick each biscuit twice with a fork.

Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until very pale golden at the edges. The biscuits should not take on much colour. Leave to cool on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack. Dust lightly with icing sugar while still warm if desired.

attrs.problem: Shortbread crumbling apart when cut or lifted
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling the dough too thin or cutting it while it is warm after baking.
attrs.fix: Keep the dough at 5 mm thickness. Leave the biscuits to cool on the tray for at least 5 minutes before moving; shortbread is very fragile when hot and firms up considerably as it cools.

attrs.problem: Biscuits spreading and losing their stamped shape
attrs.avoid: Avoid placing cut biscuits directly on a warm tray or skipping the chill.
attrs.fix: Chill the dough for the full 30 minutes. If the kitchen is warm, chill the stamped biscuits on the tray for 10 minutes before baking.
